findings.where: Article specimen, the title 'The World's Best Public-Private Partnership Law', at both widths
findings.fault: The title's apostrophe in "World's" looks like a straight typewriter tick. The rest of the article uses curly quotes and apostrophes: “What is the best…”, ‘chapter topics’, world’s. At display size the odd one out is the most visible punctuation on the article.
findings.who_objects: The founder, and Mark as a lawyer used to well-set opinions. The direction promises 'the editorial gravitas of a legal journal', and a straight quote in the headline is the typesetting slip such a reader spots first.

findings.where: Article specimen, the 'Download' label above the lecture link; worst at phone width, where it stacks the same way as 'Article page' and 'Motion'
findings.fault: The article's own 'Download' label has the same face, size, weight and colour as the tile's section labels ('Palette', 'Type pair', 'Texture', 'Article page', 'Motion'). A part inside the article looks exactly like the labels that divide the tile. On the phone it reads as the start of a new specimen section, not part of the article page.
findings.who_objects: The founder judging the tile, who needs to see where the article page ends. Angélique will copy this specimen as the article template and can't tell which label belongs to the article and which belongs to the presentation.

findings.fault: The curve is drawn in the house blue. The tile's own palette gives blue only to the wordmark, links and focus, and the direction says 'blue only on the wordmark and links'. Here blue colours something that is not a link, beside the blue links elsewhere on the sheet.
findings.who_objects: The founder, who will read the palette card's 'Wordmark, links, focus' and then see the tile break it. It weakens blue as the sign that something can be clicked.

findings.where: Motion sketch, the curve's box against its caption 'cubic-bezier(0.3, 0, 0, 1)…', at both widths
findings.fault: The curve's hairline box is set about 7 px in from the column edge, but its caption and every other specimen block start on the edge. So the box sits slightly off the left line everything else holds.
findings.who_objects: A designer or the founder scanning the specimen column. On a sheet whose whole idea is a document's exact edge, a near-miss alignment reads as careless, not intended.
